content: Acetaminophen (rectal) is an analgesic and antipyretic medication approved by the FDA for the treatment of fever and the relief of minor aches, pains, and headaches. Common adverse reactions associated with its use include itching (pruritus), constipation, nausea, vomiting, headache, agitation, insomnia, and atelectasis. Adult Indications and Dosage There is limited information available regarding the FDA-labeled indications and dosage of rectal acetaminophen in adult patients. Similarly, there is limited information on off-label uses, whether guideline-supported or not, for rectal acetaminophen in adults. Pediatric Indications and Dosage Rectal acetaminophen is FDA-approved for temporarily reducing fever and relieving minor aches, pains, and headaches in children. Directions for use: This product does not provide specific directions or complete warnings for adult use. Do not use more than directed. Remove the foil wrapper before use. Insert the suppository well into the rectum. For children aged 3–6 years: Administer 1 suppository every 4 to 6 hours as needed while symptoms persist. Do not exceed 5 suppositories in a 24-hour period. For children under 3 years of age: Consult a doctor. There is limited information on off-label uses, whether guideline-supported or not, for rectal acetaminophen in pediatric patients. Contraindications There is limited information regarding contraindications for rectal acetaminophen in the drug label. Warnings This product is for rectal use only. Liver Warning: Severe liver damage may occur if: More than 5 suppositories are used in 24 hours (the maximum daily dose). It is used in combination with other drugs containing acetaminophen. Allergy Alert: Acetaminophen may cause severe skin reactions, including: Skin reddening. Blisters. Rash. If a skin reaction occurs, discontinue use immediately and seek medical attention. Do not use: If the child is allergic to acetaminophen. With any other drug containing acetaminophen (prescription or nonprescription). If unsure, consult a doctor or pharmacist. Consult a doctor before use if the child has liver disease. Consult a doctor or pharmacist before use if the child is taking the blood-thinning drug warfarin. Discontinue use and consult a doctor if: Fever lasts more than 3 days (72 hours) or recurs. Pain persists for more than 5 days continuously. Severe or recurrent pain, or high or persistent fever, may indicate a serious illness. Postmarketing Experience: Limited information is available regarding adverse reactions reported after the product was marketed. Drug Interactions There is limited information available regarding drug interactions with rectal acetaminophen. Use in Specific Populations Pregnancy: FDA Pregnancy Category C: If pregnant or breastfeeding, consult a healthcare professional before use. There is no Australian Drug Evaluation Committee (ADEC) guidance on the use of rectal acetaminophen during pregnancy. Labor and Delivery: No FDA guidance is available on the use of rectal acetaminophen during labor and delivery. Nursing Mothers: No FDA guidance is available on the use of rectal acetaminophen in breastfeeding mothers. Pediatric Use: In case of accidental ingestion or overdose, seek medical help or contact a Poison Control Center immediately. Prompt medical attention is critical, even if no symptoms are observed. Geriatric Use: No FDA guidance is available on the use of rectal acetaminophen in elderly patients. If overdose is suspected, contact the National Poison Help hotline (1-800-222-1222) immediately. Do not use if the foil is torn or open. Storage Store at 8˚–25˚C (46˚–77˚F). Patient Counseling Information Limited information is available regarding patient counseling for rectal acetaminophen. Precautions with Alcohol The interaction between alcohol and rectal acetaminophen has not been established. Consult your doctor about the effects of consuming alcohol while using this medication.
